recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current build source satisfies the published request, and the later all-languages/starter-languages binding pattern is supported by subsequent Jira evidence; the observed spelling typo in the existing comment is editorial and not a semantic reconciliation need for this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-22694 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I request to add CapabilityStatement.acceptLanguage as a 0..* code element for servers to declare supported languages and locales usable with Accept-Language, with unsupported requests defaulting to the resource's default language.
initial_application: Commit f6fa2a5f27962062a1939c671d2345adb5cf20ad explicitly applied FHIR-22694 by adding CapabilityStatement.acceptLanguage to source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml and example acceptLanguage values to source/capabilitystatement/capabilitystatement-example.xml. Later source refactoring preserved the element in the active resource definition.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists capabilitystatement as an active resource and assigns CapabilityStatement to the conformance module, so the inspected StructureDefinition is current build source. FHIR-46074 later adopted the CapabilityStatement.acceptLanguage binding approach of required all-languages plus starter languages, explaining the current binding form despite the older FHIR-22694 resolution text saying languages value set.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source defines CapabilityStatement.acceptLanguage with min 0, max *, type code, Accept-Language guidance, required binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-languages, and a starter additional binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages; the general CapabilityStatement example includes en and es values.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied terminology issue explicitly adopted the CapabilityStatement.acceptLanguage binding approach of required all-languages plus starter languages.
